input.content:
| Step | Action | Expected Outcome |
|------|-------|------------------|
| 1 | Use multi-stage builds to separate build and runtime environments | Reduce image size by eliminating unnecessary build tools and dependencies |
| 2 | Remove unused layers and intermediate images | Minimize disk space usage and improve image consistency |
| 3 | Use minimal base images (e.g., Alpine, Ubuntu minimal) | Achieve smaller footprint without sacrificing security |
| 4 | Install only required packages and dependencies | Avoid bloat from unnecessary software |
| 5 | Cache build dependencies effectively | Speed up future builds and reduce image size |
| 6 | Validate final image size and functionality | Ensure the image runs correctly and meets performance requirements |

**Example**: 

```Dockerfile
# Stage 1: Build environment
FROM ubuntu:20.04 as builder
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential cmake
COPY . /app
WORKDIR /app
RUN cmake . && make

# Stage 2: Runtime environment
FROM alpine:latest
RUN apk add --no-cache curl wget
COPY --from=builder /app/bin/myapp /usr/local/bin/
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["myapp"]
```

**Best Practices**:
- Always use `--no-cache` when installing packages to avoid caching unnecessary files.
- Validate the final image size using `docker images` and `docker history`.
- Test the final image in a local environment before deployment.

This methodology ensures that Docker images are lightweight, secure, and efficient while preserving core functionality.

|------|-------|------------------|
| 1 | Use multi-stage builds to separate build and runtime environments | Reduce layer size by eliminating unnecessary build tools |

| 3 | Use smaller base images (e.g., Alpine, Ubuntu minimal) | Achieve smaller footprint without sacrificing security |

| 5 | Validate final image size and functionality | Ensure the image runs correctly and meets performance goals |

**Example Workflow**:
1. Start with a minimal base image (e.g., `alpine:latest`)
2. Install only required packages via `apk add` (not `apt-get`)
3. Copy only necessary files from build stage to runtime stage
4. Remove all intermediate files and cache with `RUN rm -rf /tmp/*`
5. Build and test the image with `docker build --no-cache` to verify size

**Best Practices**:
- Avoid using `docker build --cache` in production pipelines
- Regularly audit image layers with `docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} \({{.Size}}\)'`
- Monitor image size growth over time to prevent bloat
- Use `docker history` to inspect layer changes and identify large layers

| Step | Action | Key Considerations |
|------|-------|-------------------|
| 1 | Start with minimal base image (e.g., Alpine, Ubuntu minimal) | Choose image that matches application requirements |
| 2 | Use multi-stage builds to separate build and runtime environments | Only include build tools in build stage, runtime in final stage |
| 3 | Install only necessary dependencies during build | Avoid installing dev tools or unnecessary packages |
| 4 | Remove build artifacts and cache | Use `--no-cache` or `--rm` flags in Docker build |
| 5 | Use `.dockerignore` file to exclude unnecessary files | Exclude node_modules, .git, logs, etc. |
| 6 | Optimize final image with `RUN` commands | Combine commands, use `&&` to reduce layers |
| 7 | Test image size and functionality | Run `docker images` and validate app behavior |
| 8 | Push optimized image to registry | Use minimal tag names and avoid versioning in image names |

> **Best Practices**:
> - Always validate the final image works as expected
> - Keep image layers as small as possible
> - Use official base images when possible
> - Automate image optimization with CI/CD pipelines
> 
> **Example**:
> ```dockerfile
> # Build stage
> FROM node:18-alpine AS build
> WORKDIR /app
> COPY package*.json .
> RUN npm install
> 
> # Runtime stage
> FROM node:18-alpine AS runtime
> WORKDIR /app
> COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
> COPY --from=build /app/package.json .
> COPY --from=build /app/index.js .
> 
> # Final image
> FROM alpine:latest
> RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates
> COPY --from=runtime /app /app
